0.name: ACS 5-Year 2024, table S1901 — median household income by census tract
0.note: On disk. scripts/pairwise_socioeconomic_regression.py reads the same file, so the 2 analyses share one income source. The geoid is the 11-digit tract code and it matches the tract layer for 100% of tracts.

1.name: ACS 5-Year 2024, table B01003 — total population by census tract
1.note: Weights for the NTA and community-district aggregation. You cannot average medians, so those 2 layers report a population-weighted mean of the tract medians, not a median.

2.name: NYC Atomic Polygons
2.note: NOT needed. Atomic polygons would be necessary only if a census tract split across an NTA or a community district. Checked 2026-08-12: every one of the 2,325 tracts puts its interior point in exactly 1 NTA and exactly 1 community district, and no tract falls in 2 polygons. Keep this entry so the next reader knows the check happened and why the source stays unused.

3.name: NYC Building Footprints (BUILDING)
3.note: On disk, pulled 2026-04-12 by data/geo/download_nyc_buildings.py. 1,082,872 footprints and 99.1% carry a usable year; the source writes 0 for an unknown year and _proxies drops it. FacDB gives each unit a BIN, thus this is a key join and not a spatial one. WARNING: a year is NOT oriented. Every other proxy points 'higher is better', so a positive value means agreement. A positive value here says the model calls a NEWER unit better, which is a finding and not a test.
